facts.text: The Australian Pipit is a slender bird, 16 to 19 cm long, that weighs about 40 grams.
facts.quote: It is a slender bird, 16 to 19 cm long, and weighs about 40 grams.

facts.text: It is pale brown above with dark streaks, pale underparts with streaks on the breast, and a pale stripe over the eye.
facts.quote: The plumage is pale brown above with dark streaks. The underparts are pale with streaks on the breast. There is a pale stripe over the eye

facts.text: The pipit's long tail has white outer-feathers and is often wagged up and down.
facts.quote: The long tail has white outer-feathers and is often wagged up and down.

facts.text: It gives a sparrow-like chirruping call as well as a drawn-out tswee call.
facts.quote: It has a sparrow-like chirruping call and a drawn-out tswee call.

facts.text: The pipit lives in open habitats such as grassland, farmland, roadsides, dry river beds, sand dunes and open woodland.
facts.quote: It is a bird of open habitats such as grassland, farmland, roadsides, dry river beds, sand dunes and open woodland.

facts.text: It forages on the ground for beetles, spiders and insect larvae, and will also eat seeds such as those of grasses.
facts.quote: It forages on the ground for small invertebrates such as beetles, spiders and insect larvae. It will also eat seeds such as those of grasses.

facts.text: The breeding season begins in August, with the cup-shaped nest placed at the base of vegetation or in the shelter of a stone.
facts.quote: The breeding season begins in August. The cup-shaped nest is placed at the base of vegetation or in the shelter of a stone.

facts.text: The female builds the grass nest, and two to five eggs are laid, three or four being most common.
facts.quote: It is made of grass and built by the female. Two to five eggs are laid, three or four being most common.

facts.text: Its buff-white, brown-blotched eggs are incubated for 14 to 15 days, and the young can fly after 14 to 16 days.
facts.quote: They are buff-white with brown blotching and are incubated for 14 to 15 days. The young birds are fed by both parents and are able to fly after 14 to 16 days.

facts.text: The pipit was formerly grouped with other pipits as Richard's pipit before being split into separate species.
facts.quote: The Australian pipit was formerly grouped with other pipits as Richard's pipit Anthus novaeseelandiae. This species was split into Richard's, African, Mountain, Paddyfield and Australasian pipits.
